TIDEWELL SCHEDULING — SUPPORT ROUTING RULES (v3, effective 1 March 2026)

Apply the rules in order. The first rule that matches a ticket decides its queue; later rules are not considered.

Rule 1 — Security. Any ticket that reports a suspected data breach, leaked or stolen login credentials, or unauthorised access to an account goes to the Security Desk, whatever else the ticket contains.

Rule 2 — Refunds. Refund requests for $250 or less go to Tier 1 Billing. Refund requests for more than $250 go to Finance Review. Exception: if the customer's account was created fewer than 30 days before the date the ticket was received, the refund request goes to Tier 1 Billing whatever the amount, because it is covered by our 30-day money-back guarantee.

Rule 3 — Outages and bugs. If the product is unavailable for more than 50 of the customer's users, route to the Incident Bridge. Outages affecting 50 users or fewer, and all other bugs, go to Tier 2 Technical.

Rule 4 — Everything else (how-to questions, feature requests, feedback) goes to the General Queue.

Notes for agents: do not use the ticket's subject line or the priority chosen by the customer to decide routing. The customer's plan (Starter, Growth or Enterprise) does not affect routing.

Definitions: a refund request is any ticket asking for money back, including a cancellation that asks for money back. Users affected means the number of the customer's users that the ticket says cannot use the product. Account age is measured from the account creation date shown in the ticket header.

----------------------------------------
TICKET #TW-40718
Received: 20 September 2026
Customer: Oakhollow Dental Group (account created 2 September 2026, Growth plan, 64 users)
Subject: URGENT - outage!!
Priority chosen by customer: Critical

Hello,

Sorry about the dramatic subject line; the form wouldn't let me submit without picking one. Nothing is down. We had a login hiccup in our first week that your team fixed within the hour, and everything has worked since.

The real reason for this ticket: after a couple of weeks of trying Tidewell, our practice managers have decided it doesn't fit the way we schedule hygienists across our four clinics. Our hygienists rotate between sites on a fortnightly pattern, and we couldn't find a way to set that up without building every shift by hand. Your onboarding specialist was very patient with us and the patient reminder texts worked well, so this isn't a complaint about your people.

We'd like to cancel and get our money back for the annual plan we paid upfront: $1,140 in total, invoice TW-INV-22871, paid by card on 2 September.

No security concerns or anything like that; it just isn't the right tool for us. Happy to jump on a call if that helps, and let me know if you need anything else from us to process this.

Thanks,
Rosalind Achebe
Operations Director, Oakhollow Dental Group

Subject: My stay at the Vantaro Harbourside, 3–7 September

Dear Vantaro Customer Care,

I've just got back from four nights at the Vantaro Harbourside for the Nordic Logistics Summit, and I wanted to write while it's all still fresh.

First, the good parts, because there were plenty. The check-in team were lovely (Joanna upgraded me to a harbour-view room without my even asking), and the breakfast buffet was the best I've had at any conference hotel this year. The gym was clean and never crowded, and the concierge somehow found me a table at a seafood restaurant that was supposedly booked out for weeks. Please pass on my thanks to all of them. The conference facilities were excellent too: the summit organisers had the Lighthouse Suite for the main sessions, and your AV team sorted out a projector problem on the first morning in under five minutes. Lunch was served on time every day, which at a 300-person event is no small achievement.

The less good part: on the second night there was a wedding party in the courtyard below my room until well after 1am. I rang reception, who were apologetic and sent up earplugs, which helped a little. I'm mentioning it for your records rather than to complain. These things happen at busy hotels, and I'm not asking for any kind of compensation.

Now, the thing I actually need help with. My employer only reimburses travel against an invoice that shows the company's name and VAT number. The invoice I was handed at checkout is made out to me personally and has no VAT number on it, so our finance team has rejected my expense claim. They have confirmed that the amount itself is correct; only the name and VAT details need to change. Could you please reissue the invoice for the whole stay (folio 55-20931, total €1,248.60) addressed to:

Tidemark Haulage Ltd
VAT number: IE 3345127KH
14 Quay Street, Galway

Our expense deadline is the 30th, so the sooner the better.

A couple of other small things, just so you have the whole picture. I thought I'd left my laptop charger plugged in beside the desk, but it turned up in the lining of my suitcase when I unpacked, so there's no need to search the room. And I've checked that my Vantaro Circle points for the stay have posted: all 4,990 of them are there, so no action is needed on that either.

I'm already planning to come back for next year's summit, and I'll book directly with you once the dates are announced. Thanks again to the whole team; apart from the one noisy night, it was a genuinely lovely stay.

Kind regards,
Helena Marsh

Hi Liam,

Three things, roughly in order of pain.

1. Since Friday 28 August, our public API, which sits behind your eu-west load balancer, has been returning intermittent 502 Bad Gateway errors: about 3–5% of requests at peak, clustered around 09:00–11:00 and 14:00–16:00 CET. Our backend instances look healthy the whole time (CPU under 40%, no restarts, nothing unusual in the application logs). Our own customers are starting to notice: we handle about 2.4 million API calls a day for around 140 retail clients, and our SLA to them is 99.5%, so this is starting to cost us credits of our own.

2. Your status page puts eu-west availability for August at 99.62%. Our contract has a 99.9% monthly availability SLA with service credits, so we'd like to claim the credit we're owed.

3. Our new data protection officer needs a countersigned copy of our data processing agreement for the audit file. We can only find the unsigned version from 2024.

One more thing: someone on your side mentioned on a call that moving to the Performance tier might 'make the 502s go away'. I'd rather understand the root cause before we talk about spending more money.

Renata

---
From: Sunita Rao (Support Engineer, Cobaltix Cloud)
Sent: Mon 31 Aug 2026, 10:47

Hi Renata,

I've picked up the 502s under ticket CBX-58214. In the load balancer logs, the errors line up with upstream connections being closed by your instances while requests are still in flight. The most common cause is a mismatch between the load balancer's idle timeout (60 seconds) and your application's keep-alive timeout (30 seconds on your instances).

Could you raise the keep-alive timeout on your instances to 75 seconds? That way the load balancer always closes idle connections first. I'll keep the ticket open while we monitor.

Sunita

---
From: Renata Oyelaran
Sent: Mon 31 Aug 2026, 11:58

Thanks, Sunita. A few sample request IDs from this morning's failures, in case they help: 7f3a-91c2 (09:14:07 CET), 7f3a-a0d8 (09:31:52), 7f3b-0c11 (10:02:19) and 7f3b-2e7f (10:47:33). All four hit node lb-euw-2, but we've seen failures on the other two nodes as well. We'll make the keep-alive change on Wednesday morning, when traffic is lowest.

Renata

From: Liam Brodeur
Sent: Mon 31 Aug 2026, 13:15

Thanks for setting it all out so clearly. Sunita has the 502s. On the other two points:

- SLA credit: credits are calculated and applied by our Billing team, not by account management. I've forwarded your claim to them with the August availability figure. For reference, the credit bands in your contract are 10% of the monthly fee for availability from 99.0% up to 99.9%, and 25% below 99.0%.
- DPA: I've asked Pieter in our legal team to send you a countersigned copy.

And fair point on the Performance tier; no pressure from me.

Liam

Sent: Mon 31 Aug 2026, 14:20

Thanks, Renata, those IDs are useful. All four requests were sent on reused connections that your backend had closed after 30 seconds of idle time, which fits the timeout theory. I've also checked the three nodes (lb-euw-1, lb-euw-2 and lb-euw-3): they all show the same pattern, so it isn't a single bad node. Wednesday morning works. After you make the change, please don't restart the load balancer; the new keep-alive will take effect as connections recycle.

Sunita

Renata
